The goal is to deepen the understanding of these effects to advance the development of strategies and technologies that protect distribution networks, particularly in scenarios that involve IIDG.

articleTitle: Transient Recovery Voltage Effects in Circuit Breakers Involved in Series-Connected Air Core Reactors
abstract: Transient Recovery Voltage (TRV) effect has an impact in circuit breakers regarding to high voltage grids involved with high short circuit, especially in air-core reactors applications, because of explosions occurred in circuit breakers during the last years; caused by TRV effect over these devices. This research has a novel contribution with a new proposal improvement, for the international standard as lEC 62271-100:2020 [1], with the selection criteria to mitigate the TRV effect, for limiting short circuit in air-core reactors, verifying, and the efficiency in a real case study in Peru. In this model, we proposed an equivalent of air core reactor, with simulations and real data validations, performed for different approaches, with improvement for the international standards.

articleTitle: Impact of Augmented Reality on the Teaching of Anatomy: A Study in Health Sciences Students
abstract: In the domain of health sciences education, the integration of innovative educational technologies is indispensable for enhancing the comprehension of anatomical concepts. This study explores the impact of Augmented Reality (AR) on anatomy education, specifically focusing on the upper limb. The aim is to assess how AR influences learning outcomes, student engagement, and motivation. Forty-two students from the Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Cauca actively participated in the study. The findings reveal a significant preference for frequent utilization of educational technologies among the participants, showcasing a high level of technological integration in their learning practices. The tool's ease of use and its substantial impact on improving the understanding of upper limb anatomy received positive feedback, with an average rating of 4.5 on a scale of 0 from 5. This study demonstrates that AR, when implemented in anatomy education for health sciences students, not only improves understanding but also fosters motivation and engagement. These results underscore the potential of AR as a transformative tool in health sciences education, offering an immersive and interactive learning experience that aligns with the preferences and needs of actual generation learners.

articleTitle: WiFi Lab Guide UDFJC
abstract: This document presents the details of development of laboratory practices set with the ANRITSU MS2830A, that is a measurement equipment of electronics lab “Universidad Distrital Francisco Jose de Caldas”, generating laboratory guides that allow students, teachers and researchers to execute projects with measurements and that involve the analysis, transmission and reception of Wi- Fi signals that comply with the IEEE 802.11 standard, all based on experimentation of theoretical-practical concepts that are been reviewed throughout the Telecommunications Engineering courses and which can be strengthened through the execution of laboratory practices through the use of guides. A set of seven laboratory guides were generated, which were tested through a pilot plan with students.

articleTitle: Application of a Squirrel Cage Induction Machine as a Dynamometer for Motor Heat-run Tests
abstract: The paper documents the application of a three- phase induction machine as a dynamometer in a three-phase motor testing experiment, wherein the motor is required to be fully loaded. Two similarly sized induction machines were used for the experiment, with the output power of the induction motor matching the required input mechanical power of an induction generator. Two low-cost methods of achieving a dynamometer load were tested. One method was through using a self-excited induction generator (SEIG) setup with an electrical load made of commercial heater strips. The capacitance providing the excitation was estimated using theoretical calculations, but it was found to be insufficient for fully loading the SEIG. The second method was by supplying both machines with low-cost variable frequency drives (VFDs) with one VFD operating in regenerative braking mode with braking resistors to provide the necessary dynamometeric load to the other machine. It was found that the motor loading could be controlled by adjusting the supply frequency of one machine relative to the other machine. However, some complications arose with preventing inadvertent overloads and tripping which will be discussed.

articleTitle: Implementation of a MouseTrap Car as a Teaching Tool to Study Damped Oscillations
abstract: The MouseTrap Car (MC) is a manually crafted vehicle that operates using stored potential energy in a spring. The MC has traditionally served as a valuable tool in STEM environments for experimentally explaining physical phenomena such as energy conservation and motion. This paper presents a novel implementation of the MC as a device capable of demonstrating damped oscillations, serving as an educational tool for modeling this type of motion. A didactic sequence has been designed utilizing the MC to study the characteristics of damped motion through active learning methodologies.

articleTitle: Waze for Cities: An Effective Alternative for Traffic Study
abstract: This study explores the use of crowdsourcing data, specifically those provided by Waze for Cities, to obtain vehicular traffic data for the city of Cuenca to be used in mobility planning. A detailed methodology is presented that includes data extraction and preprocessing, as well as visualization through a dashboard and generation of a heat map. The usefulness of Waze as an agile and low-cost alternative to understand vehicular behavior in cities is highlighted.

articleTitle: Application for Secure Password Self-Service Management in Local Active Directory (AD) Environments
abstract: The Windows Server Active Directory (AD) in a local environment (on-premises) works as a Domain Controller, one of the most important services it provides is the authentication of users. The AD on-premises does not provide mechanisms for local self-service user passwords and is a major feature needed in a help desk service. There are companies that provide these services, but at high implementation costs and annual subscriptions. Therefore, this paper proposes a web application that enables the self-service of user passwords reducing costs considerably and making the process more practical and convenient for end users and system administrators. It must also provide security guarantees in the handling of sensitive data such as passwords, tokens, emails, which are included and discussed.

articleTitle: Nanoparticle-Bearing Chitosan Implants for in Situ Stem Cell Reprogramming
abstract: To repopulate the injured or damaged tissue with functional cells, the extracorporeal reprogramming and replantation of the stem cells look like promising approach, but it is highly time and effort consuming, especially when optimal window for surgical intervention comes into regard. It brings us to the idea of generating the stem cells directly at the site of injury by reprogramming the surrounding and migrating cells into stem cells with locally delivered set of transforming factors. Here we are demonstrating a pilot implant assembly from the set of the functional materials: chitosan/glycol-chitosan/DNA nanoparticles (C/G/D NP) and the chitosan derivates with MRI-contrast. Presented structures and materials were well tolerated during in vitro tests and were able to initialize the reprogramming in primary rat fibroblasts. When implanted in rats they were traceable by MRI, mechanically sound, and did not cause adverse local or general responses. In the vicinity of the implantation site, we could detect GFP- and Nanog-positive cells suggesting initialization of reprogramming. During both in vitro and in vivo treatments, the number of induced Nanog-positive cells was independent from age of the implant recipient.

articleTitle: Generative AI for Consumer Communications: Classification, Summarization, Response Generation
abstract: Generative AI showed the unexpected power of large language models (LLMs) for understanding and generation of natural language text and other modalities at the end of 2022. This paper presents a novel generative AI system for text classification, summarization and response generation of consumer communications. The system uses the same foundation model and a uniform pipeline for the tasks proposed. Consumer communications are massive and served mainly via voice and text, and until recently could be handled only with human agents (customer service representatives). However, they must be handled with quality, consistency, speed and low cost, at scale. We limit our attention to financial consumer communications from the U.S. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB), publicly available in a dataset of over 4.7 million complaints. Performance reaches 88 % accuracy (without fine-tuning) for classification and over 72 % for summarization and response generation. Artificial intelligence has great positive impacts for business and society, but its application and deployment also poses risks and unknowns. We thus address the important questions of risk, bias, interpretability, explainability, safety and regulatory compliance with the emerging legal frameworks.

articleTitle: Robust Collision-Free Guidance for Multicopters in Airspaces with Numerous Flying Obstacles
abstract: This paper proposes a robust guidance for mul-tirotor aerial vehicles with uncertain dynamics and equipped with short-range detection sensors in scenarios with multiple accelerated obstacles and velocity constraints. To handle the uncertain dynamics in the guidance level, the position and velocity admissible sets are tightened according to the respective inner-loop tracking errors. Moreover, a hybrid prescribed-time arbitrary-order differentiator is used to estimate the obstacles' velocities and accelerations using the sensor readings. Based on these estimates, we build a set of possible future positions for the obstacles, and use this set to calculate a robust collision-free position command for the vehicle. The proposed method is experimentally evaluated using a mixed-reality setup composed of a Crazyflie quad copter, motion capture cameras, and virtual obstacles. The results show that the proposed method is viable for real-time implementation and effective in providing collision avoidance and satisfying velocity constraints.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity Maturity Model Against Ransomware Attacks for the Financial Sector
abstract: Financial microenterprises are essential for a country's economic development; however, they face significant cybersecurity challenges due to the prevalence of ransomware, which accounted for 23% of all security incidents in 2020. This study proposes a Ransomware Attack Mitigation Maturity Model for the financial sector to reduce such attacks. The model consists of 6 maturity levels and 20 established domains, which are weighted and displayed on a results dashboard. The proposed model was validated by expert judgment within the financial and information security sectors. Results show that the model is highly effective in identifying vulnerabilities (93.33%) and recognizing security gaps (83.33%), with a high degree of satisfaction from security personnel (90.00%). This model offers a solid foundation for strengthening cybersecurity and protecting financial microenterprises, thereby contributing to economic development.

articleTitle: Automation of Tribological Analysis of Mining Equipment through Machine Learning
abstract: In recent years, artificial intelligence has been gaining ground in various fields, and the mining industry is no exception. This article presents a comparative analysis of different machine learning techniques applied to the tribological analysis of mechanical equipment components. Machine learning-based approaches are considered promising for increasing safety and optimizing preventive maintenance schedules, thereby extending the lifespan of mining equipment. For this, oil analysis is crucial. In the project, a methodology based on statistical tests was used to determine anomalies in oil samples. On the other hand, subjective interpretations by those responsible for the analysis lead to significant errors and unscheduled equipment shutdowns. Implementing machine learning promises to automate and refine this analysis, allowing for more accurate and earlier detection of potential failures, thus increasing equipment reliability. Various machine learning algorithms will be evaluated to develop an anomaly detection model for oil samples and a classification model for the component's condition based on its oil sample.

articleTitle: A Sharper Look: Edge Detection and Light-Weight 3D Vision Transformers for Parkinsonian Disorder Classification on MRI Imaging
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurological disorder that affects motor function and is often accompanied by non-motor symptoms, including impulse control disorders (ICDs) and apathy. Early and accurate diagnosis and treatment of ICDs are crucial for improving patient outcomes. This research investigates the advantages of using deep learning and edge detection filter for anatomical pattern recognition associated with Parkinsonian Disorders. We used three transformer-based architectures to analyze the preprocessed MRI T1 weighted images and to compare the strengths and weaknesses of each architecture. The Edge detection filter improves the model accuracy and efficiency for all architectures. The MobileViT-3D achieves a top-1 accuracy of 99.13% on a dataset of 3D MRI images, demonstrating its potential as a promising approach for anatomical pattern recognition associated to PD-related disorders.

articleTitle: Deep Learning Approaches for Rust Identification in Ecuadorian Agriculture
abstract: While the agricultural sector is one of Ecuador's strongest and largest sectors, with coffee being an important part of this industry; however, production constraints and the prevalence of coffee leaf rust disease have inhibited the sector from achieving its full potential output. To address this issue, this study investigates seven Deep Neural Network architectures utilizing Transfer Learning to distinguish coffee leaf rust on crops across different infection levels. The top-performing model, InceptionResNetV2, achieved an accuracy of 93.84%, solidifying its leading position in this emerging field. Inception V3closely followed with an accuracy of 93.09%, demonstrating its effectiveness in rust identification with a minimal error rate of 6.16%. Notably, InceptionResNetV2 exhibited superior generalization ability, achieving an F1-score of 93.73%. However, some models showed limitations in recall rates for specific classes, highlighting the importance of decisions made in model design, data characteristics, and hyper-parameters settings in determining the model performance. These findings suggest potential avenues for future research and emphasize the promising role of advanced Machine Learning and Deep Learning techniques in enhancing crop management and agricultural economies.

articleTitle: Frame Deletion Detection in Videos Using Convolutional Neural Networks
abstract: With the broad adoption of digital media, videos are susceptible to various forms of forgery, making it crucial to ensure their authenticity, especially since they serve as digital evidence in contexts such as courts or forensic investigations. One of the main forgeries is frame deletion, which consists of removing frames from a video to hide specific actions from the human eye. Therefore, ways to automate and reduce errors when detecting frame deletion in videos are necessary, specially when analyzing a large volume of videos. We measure the performance of two Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) approaches for detecting frame deletion: a supervised 3DCNN model and an unsupervised model based on the VGG-16 architecture. We evaluated them in terms of accuracy, precision, recall and F1 score, using the following datasets: UCF-101, VIFFD and DTD (Driving Test Dataset), a dataset of authentic and forged driving test videos as our own contribution to the data community. Afterwards, we discuss the results and propose directions for future research in this area.

articleTitle: Application of Augmented Reality and Its Impact on the Historical and Cultural Management of a Tourist Center in Northern Peru
abstract: The need to incorporate innovative technologies to facilitate access to historical information, enrich the visitor experience, encourage public participation and increase the value of cultural heritage was the justification for this study. The main objective was to measure the impact of the implementation of an augmented reality application in the historical and cultural management of the Cajamarca Hydrangea Garden in the year 2023. The research was experimental with a quantitative approach, using the survey technique and the questionnaire instrument. In the development of the software, the agile Scrum framework was adopted, using HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend, the Python language, AR libraries and Django for the backend. After the implementation of the application, an increase was observed in the evaluated dimensions: 54% in information dissemination, 19% in visitor experience, 300% in reporting effectiveness, 55% in reservation efficiency and in the quality of the service. application 80% in functionality, 71 % in usability, 67% in efficiency, 64% in portability and 75% in security. These results reflect a positive impact derived from the implementation of the application in this study.

articleTitle: Portable Colposcopic Device Based On Artificial Intelligence
abstract: The following article presents the development of a low-cost digital colposcopy device designed to fit a wide range of speculum sizes, offering 99 % diagnostic accuracy. The main objective is to provide an affordable alternative to conventional colposcopy systems, which typically range in price from US $9,000 to US $12,000. Traditional colposcopy has been shown by studies to be limited in its diagnostic accuracy. This technique, based on visual interpretation by an experienced gynecologist, only achieves 80 % accuracy compared to histological results. In response to this difficulty, the developed device merges two technologies: the analysis by spectrography, adding RGB LEDs that will modify the contrast of the acetowhitening effect of the cervix, and the incorporation of a transformers based artificial intelligence algorithm, designed for multi-class images classification. In conclusion, the proposed low-cost portable colposcope offers a significant advance in cervical pathology detection, providing high diagnostic accuracy comparable to conventional systems at a fraction of the cost. This innovation has the potential to greatly impact marginalized communities or resource-limited regions without access to affordable diagnostic tools or the presence of highly skilled personnel.

articleTitle: Development of an Intelligent Irrigation System for a Rose Cultivation Based on IoT
abstract: One of the most challenges rose farmers face are the optimization of the usage of water, being irrigation a critical issue for agriculture. Conventional irrigation methods could be inefficient affecting the quality and yield of the rose crop. In this work an IoT-based smart irrigation system for roses was implemented. The system involves sensors and communication devices known as node, actuators, and a central control system. The system initiates the process by the measurement of soil moisture and temperature through sensors, data is preprocesed and transmitted by LoRaWAN technology by the Cube-Cell module to be connected to the Chirpstack platform. Finally users can visualize on an OLED display. For testing the solution, three nodes were used, locating them in specific places in a greenhouse. To save energy nodes were configured in the low power consumption mode and low polling mode for transmision. Details of the implementation are presented in the work.

articleTitle: On the Equivalence Between Mixed-Integer Linear and Linear Programming Problems in MPC for Photovoltaic Plants with Energy Storage
abstract: This paper investigates the equivalence between a class of mixed-integer linear and linear programming prob-lems. By utilizing the addition of slack variables theorem, we demonstrate that certain optimization problems arising in Model Predictive Control strategies, which involve logical constraints, can be solved as linear programming problems. Consequently, the equivalent linear programming problem can be solved using the standard and numerically efficient method named the Sim-plex method, as opposed to mixed-integer linear programming problems for which the best solution method is not clear. As a case study, we address the control problem of photovoltaic plants with energy storage systems. We design a model-based predictive control scheme based on our proposed equivalent linear programming problem to maximize economic benefits derived from energy delivered by both photovoltaic panels and energy storage systems to the grid in a deregulated electricity market, achieved by managing the charge and discharge of the energy storage. Additionally, the proposed scheme allows for the consideration of rate-based variable efficiency in the energy stor-age system model, offering a more comprehensive implementation compared to the previous approach in the literature, where only an ideal battery was considered. Furthermore, simulations reveal that the proposed control methodology reduces the execution time of model-predictive control iterations compared to another approach based on mixed-integer linear programming schemes with similar considerations, thereby enhancing the scalability of the solution.

articleTitle: A Meta-Analysis of Blockchain Acceptance Research and New Theory Directions
abstract: Blockchain, through its secure distributed ledger technology, has been heralded as an important enabler of consumer and business applications. In addition to cryptocurrency, there are many examples of existing and planned implementations of blockchain-enabled systems in organizations, such as in the supply chain. However, what is unclear from the literature, are the mechanisms driving the acceptance of blockchain systems and the extent to which salient models of technology acceptance are capable of explaining adoption behavior. This research employs large-scale meta-SEM analysis using 37,865 respondents from 142 data sets to examine critically a variety of competing models of blockchain technology acceptance. The results identify two new models that help to explain a significant amount of variance in behavioral intention to use blockchain systems, trust-risk model (TRM) and a TRM/UTAUT2 hybrid TRAUT. Thus, although we find support for the standard models of acceptance, the paper suggests that new models incorporating trust and risk are essential in the blockchain context. The models are robust to tests using a variety of moderators of relationships.

articleTitle: A Heterogeneous Multi-RISCV Architecture for Image Processing and Computer Vision Applications
abstract: In the advanced field of Image Processing and Computer Vision (IP/CV), there is a trend toward utilising parallel processing in computer architectures for enhanced efficiency, striking a balance between general-purpose capabilities and hardware-specific processes. The RISC-V standard, now backed by a wide array of compilers, frameworks, and operating systems, is paving the way for innovative cores. Our introduction of a Multi-Processor Systems on Chip (MPSoC), MPRISC-V, is a testament to this evolution. This system incorporates a Network on Chip (No <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex>) for robust intra-chip communication. The Processing System (PS) seamlessly integrates and manages it through a user-friendly API crafted to simplify the development cycle. To ascertain its effectiveness, we tested it on a Zynq Ultrascale+ MPSoC device, deploying a Sobel-based application benchmark. By evaluating its efficiency in terms of cycles/pixels, our findings underscore its potential and spotlight areas ripe for further enhancement.

articleTitle: Efficiency Calculation for a 90 MVA Vertical Shaft Hydro-Alternator using the Calorimetric Method
abstract: This paper presents the development of an algorithm to measure the efficiency of a salient-pole synchronous generator using a calorimetric method based on the standards IEC 60034- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2\mathrm{A}$</tex>, IEC 60034-2-1:2007, and IEC 60034-2-2:2010. This indirect method is based on the principle that all the losses in the generator are dissipated as heat. The article describes the methodology used to develop and implement the algorithm in a 90 MW vertical shaft synchronous machine, as well as the instrumentation required to measure the necessary variables. Finally, a comparison is made between the results obtained from the implemented algorithm to determine the efficiency and the corresponding report provided by the manufacturer of the equipment.

articleTitle: Strategies for Future Education: An Initial Analysis of Learning Platform Mechanics and Interfaces
abstract: This article presents a preliminary analysis that explores the trans formative potential of integrating game mechanics and user interfaces into digital educational platforms, widely recognized as gamification. We focus on general aspects such as heuristic evaluations, cross-platform accessibility, aesthetic design, and strategic use of educational materials. This initial review illustrates how these elements collectively enhance the learning experience. To carry out the exercise, different educational platforms were considered, and each one was analyzed regarding its general behavior and available educational material. Through this exercise, we were able to identify the best practices that should be integrated into the development of future platforms or the improvement of the current ones. The article suggests that future comprehensive studies could further revolutionize the educational landscape by creating more adaptive and responsive learning environments by seamlessly integrating game design, pedagogy, and digital tools.

articleTitle: User Centered Design Methods in Software Development: A Case Study in a Peruvian Office of Financial Aid and Scholarships
abstract: This paper presents a case study where User-Centered Design (UCD) methodologies were employed to develop a software solution. Techniques used, such as interviews with users and the creation of user personas, will be described as an approach to understanding the needs and expectations of end users. This study focuses on the Office of Scholarships and Tutoring at the Pontifical Catholic University of Peru. This office relies on numerous non-integrated tools in its day-to-day operations, leading to manual and repetitive tasks. A software solution is then thought of as an alternative to streamline these processes, improving the user experience for the office's workers and clients. The development of this system was carried on by adopting UCD techniques. The developed software was evaluated by 12 test users who performed a specific task, followed by interviews and a System Usability Scale (SUS) based questionnaire. The results indicated that all users successfully completed their objectives and found the system simple to use. Even though some design flaws were detected, the software scored 82.29 in the SUS scale.

articleTitle: Distributed Edge Computing for Appearance-Based Gait Recognition
abstract: The expansion of smart cities requires the integration of advanced security technologies, including gait recognition, which is increasingly valued for enhancing urban surveillance. This paper introduces a novel distributed edge computing framework specifically designed for appearance-based real-time gait recognition, utilizing deep learning techniques to ensure efficient and accurate analysis. The framework leverages a distributed architecture that minimizes latency and distributes computational loads across multiple devices, effectively balancing processing demands. We also introduce the OAKGait16 dataset, which comprises video sequences of various individuals from multiple view angles and in different clothing variants, providing a robust basis for comprehensive analysis. Our evaluations demonstrate that our approach not only achieves high efficiency and accuracy in controlled settings-but also keeps the processing speed at 29 frames per second, showcasing its potential for real-world application in smart city security systems. This work establishes a foundational framework intended to guide further advancements in practical, scalable gait recognition systems.

articleTitle: CPT-based Active Power Filter with Repetitive Controller and Capacitor Voltage Feedforward under Non-Ideal Grid
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a repetitive controller along with capacitor voltage feedforward applied to an LCL filter active power filter (APF). The repetitive controller can operate in systems with disturbances exhibiting high harmonic content and the feedforward action can reshape the output impedance of the APF. The conservative power theory (CPT) is proposed to obtain reference signals for the purpose of total mitigation of unwanted currents. The proposed technique ensures that only the active current flows through the electrical grid, while maintaining the stability of the APF-grid system through passivity theory. Finally, the proposed control strategy is validated using the Matlab/Simulink® software under several conditions of grid imbalances and harmonic distortions.

articleTitle: Method to Evaluate the Ampacity of Underground Cables in Medium-Voltage Electrical Networks in Operation
abstract: This paper presents a method to evaluate the ampacity of medium-voltage underground cables, which takes into account the construction of a terrain thermal resistivity map, the route of the medium voltage feeders, the modeling of the cable, the modeling of the installation characteristics, and the information of the amperage passing through the feeder obtained from the SCADA system. This method includes the processing of the information in its own software created in Visual Studio and programmed in Visual Basic, which takes as a calculation basis both the IEC 60287 standard for stationary load regime and the IEC 60853 standard for cyclic load regime. This method is applied for an electric distribution company in Peru, evaluating the ampacity for a section of a feeder.

articleTitle: Network Traffic Analysis Through Flows and Packets with Machine Learning
abstract: This study investigates cybersecurity in IoT networks by analyzing MQTT traffic through flow-based records to detect anomalies and improve security measures. The methodology includes Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) and the application of machine learning models to differentiate between benign and malicious traffic, explicitly focusing on brute-force attacks. Furthermore, a comparative analysis between flow-level and packet-level features reveals that flow-level features are more effective for classification tasks. This analysis improves the understanding of traffic behavior and contributes to the development of robust intrusion detection systems.

articleTitle: Differentiation Price Mechanism for Loss Minimization in Peer-to-Peer Local Energy Markets
abstract: The increasing adoption of distributed energy re-sources (DERs) has led to a new trend in reshaping electric-ity markets using peer-to-peer (P2P) transactive energy (TE) approaches. These methods enable participants to engage in energy trading to align demand with the supply of various energy resources and services. However, they present challenges regarding techno-economic efficiency and fairness assurance. In this context, effectively integrating the physical and virtual layers within a P2P framework is crucial to achieving techno-economic goals, though identifying appropriate models is not straight-forward. This article addresses this challenge by proposing a pricing mechanism to differentiate similar products offered in a DC power distribution system. It demonstrates how losses could serve as a suitable price differentiator to promote localized consumption, while also proving that a wide range of techno-economic criteria could determine loss allocation.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Via Nonlinear Model Predictive Control for Thermal Process with Variable Longtime Delay
abstract: The main concern in thermal process control revolves around uncertainties and disturbances, arising from external processes, unmodeled dynamics, or simplified characteristics, to name a few. For instance, a primary source of uncertainties involves disturbances and long-time delays, which typically lead to loose robust control performance. This paper develops a robust control technique based on Reinforcement-Learning (RL) strategies via Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG), integrating Nonlinear Model Predictive Control (NMPC). The NMPC works as a policy generator and the DDPG strategy is devoted to evaluating the learning process. While NMPC was able to approach tracking performance, the combined scheme with DDPG allowed further robust performance in terms of adaptation to changing thermal process conditions such as external disturbances and variations to internal model parameters. Indeed, combining strategies (NMPC-based DDPG) rendered unnecessary offline design of a terminal cost and constraints typically required in traditional robustified NMPC strategies. The RL agent was trained, tested, and validated in a simulation environment using a thermal process with longtime delay. Results demonstrated that the proposed NMPC-based DDPG technique achieved nearly similar tracking performance compared to traditional NMPC strategies, even maintaining control objectives. However, the proposed control strategy exhibited enhanced adaptivity regarding NMPC under the presence of disturbances and model parameter variations. The latter findings are expected to have an impact on the energy resources of real thermal processes in the industry.

articleTitle: Comparing Multi-Objective Surrogate Models for Binary Petroleum Well Placement
abstract: Optimization problems often involve expensive computational calculations. For example, in petroleum well place-ment problems, optimization techniques are applied to reservoir simulation models to identify the optimal number and positions of exploration wells. Each evaluation of a well placement plan requires extensive calculations of differential equations to forecast fluid behavior. To enhance the quality of the optimization techniques without increasing the computational burden, re-searchers have explored combining optimization methods with Surrogate Models, approximation techniques used in regression problems to replace expensive objective functions with more computationally efficient evaluations. However, since most of the research on surrogate modeling has been performed for single-objective problems, surrogate modeling for multi-objective problems remains a challenging task. For this reason, this paper provides a comparative analysis of three supervised learning techniques, Random Forest (RF), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) when applied as multi-objective surrogate models to approximate the real objective function val-ues of five datasets of a real-world expensive discrete petroleum well placement problem. We also investigate if an ensemble of these three methods surpasses their individual performances. The results demonstrate that the ensemble prediction outperforms the individual methods in 4 out of 5 datasets in terms of Root Mean Square Error, while k-NN provides the best Mean Absolute Error in 4 out of 5 datasets. Nonetheless, the Friedman and Bonferroni-Dunn tests indicate that there are only statistically significant differences between MLP and the remaining methods. Therefore, the choice between k-NN, RF, or the ensemble is indifferent.

articleTitle: Exploring Supervised and Unsupervised Learning Techniques to Detect Ground-Glass Opacities in CT Images for COVID-19
abstract: In the continuous effort to mitigate the impacts of coronavirus disease (COVID-19) on global health, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising ally, offering potential breakthroughs in the diagnosis and prognosis of lung diseases. Indeed, the use of supervised and unsupervised learning methods has the potential to aid in clinical decision-making and contribute to the comprehension of novel diseases. This study provides a comparative analysis of unsupervised and supervised methodolo-gies for accurately identifying ground-glass opacity (GGO) areas in CT scans. The GGO pulmonary lesion acts as a key diagnos-tic indicator of COVID-19 infection. Given the labor-intensive process of manually segmenting large chest CT datasets, there is an urgent requirement for dependable automated methods that facilitate efficient analysis of chest CT anatomy within extensive research databases. This need is particularly pronounced for less frequently annotated areas, such as pulmonary consolidations and radiological findings such as GGO lesions. To tackle this challenge, our study evaluates the performance of supervised and unsupervised learning methods using dice score, precision, and accuracy metrics. The evaluations are conducted on various datasets of annotated CT scans from COVID-19 patients. We consider that these findings are important in the context of COVID-19 diagnosis from CT scans and the relevance of both supervised and unsupervised learning techniques. Finally, we offer the open-source code of the experiments carried out in the research at https://github.com/gicc-lab/gicc_aimdai.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Safety in Lithium Battery Energy Storage: A Comprehensive Review
abstract: Safety in energy storage power plants using batteries is a critically important issue, especially as electrochemical storage technologies are increasingly adopted. However, battery management systems face challenges in accurately collecting data on individual cell status, which hinders effective verification of their performance. In this regard, the use of machine learning techniques emerges as a promising solution by enabling the prediction of lithium-ion battery operating conditions. This study takes an in-depth look at the risks associated with battery misuse and its potential consequences, such as thermal runaway, and explores how machine learning techniques can improve safety by considering factors such as heat generation rate and battery health status at a more detailed and accurate level.

articleTitle: RSSI-Based Indoor Localization Using Machine Learning for Wireless Sensor Networks: A Recent Review
abstract: The significance of device localization has increased in response to the current challenges of indoor positioning systems. This need is particularly severe in wireless sensor networks, where node awareness of its location within the sensor field is advantageous for tasks such as event monitoring. Numerous review papers have categorized indoor localization algorithms using conventional machine learning methods. However, limited attention has been devoted to works incorporating alternative classification schemes and considering learning-based localization systems, as proposed in this study. This paper introduces a review of indoor localization machine learning approaches to extend the discussion by focusing on learning models that dynamically update with each new data point received, categorizing approaches into fingerprinting and trilateration techniques from received signal strength indicators. Thus, the proposed study lays the foundation for future research endeavors in indoor localization, especially those integrating incremental learning and continuously updating models with new data.

articleTitle: Enhancing LoRaWAN RSSI Prediction Accuracy with Weather-Aware Machine Learning Models
abstract: This investigation compares the prediction accuracy of three baseline machine learning (ML) models and our proposed model combining Random Forest and Multi-Layer Perceptron (RF-MLP) to predict received signal strength indicator (RSSI) in a LoRaWAN network, with and without using climate data. The ML models are Random Forest (RF), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). All models were tested in a maize crop setting, using weather variables such as humidity, temperature, solar radiation, and the terminal nodes' geographical coordinates and height as input features. The result shows that MLP performs better than RF and LSTM when predicting the RSSI values of a newly inserted node in the network. On the other hand, the RF model performed the best when forecasting future RSSI values of a single node. The proposed RF-MLP achieved the best performance overall. Also, ML models improved their performance when using climate data, compared to when it was excluded as input, with a maximum improvement level of 46.8%.

articleTitle: Impact of the Implementation of an Information System in the Management of Materials Tickets in a Telecommunications and Systems Company
abstract: The company Intelsi S.A.C. It presented dispersion of relevant information for materials management between spreadsheets and documents, making decision making difficult. The general objective of the research was to measure the impact of implementing an information system for materials ticket management. The methodology consisted of applying pre-and post-implementation questionnaires to a sample of supervisors to evaluate variables using descriptive statistics before and compare subsequent results with statistical tests. The initial analyzes revealed opportunities for improvement in variables such as waiting times and level of satisfaction in the processes. After implementing the information system, an improvement was observed in the organization of management processes, with faster and centralized access to relevant information, which facilitated decision making. After the implementation of the technological tool, it was possible to centralize all the key data to manage the materials digitally. This made it possible to streamline procedures and strengthen management through a single point of access to updated data. In conclusion, the implementation of the system had a positive impact on organizational processes through the optimization of resources and simplification of tasks, favoring more effective management of materials tickets in the company.

articleTitle: Assesment of Frequency Response Uncertainty on Power Systems with RES
abstract: The integration of non-conventional renewable energy sources (RES) into the electrical grid has significantly increased to mitigate global warming and reduce costs. However, RES, connected through converters, impact system inertia, increasing the rate of change of frequency (RoCoF) and potentially exceeding frequency limits. Uncertainties due to factors like solar radiation directly affect injected power, emphasizing the need to assess operational capability. This study uses the probabilistic technique 2m+1 Point Estimate Method (PEM) to model power injection from RES and assess frequency response through indices like steady-state frequency, RoCoF, and Nadir. Probabilistic load flow analysis and transient stability studies determine expected values, standard deviations, confidence intervals, and regulatory compliance probabilities to assess the frequency uncertainty in the power system. The study, using the PST-16 system adapted to the Colombian context, highlights the impact of RES on frequency response, with potential regulatory non-compliance. It underscores the need for corrective measures and proposes the use of virtual inertia to mitigate RES effects on system dynamics, aiding energy transition planning.

articleTitle: Feature Selection for Forecasting of Energy Spot Price in the Colombian Market
abstract: Enhancing the forecasting accuracy of energy spot prices is vital for decision-making in energy trading. This study evaluates various feature selection methods and regression models to predict energy prices in Colombia. We compare Principal Components Analysis, Pearson Correlation Coefficients, Mutual Information, and Least Absolute Shrinkage methods with Ran-dom Forest, Extra Gradient boost, and CatBoost models. Mutual Information is the most compelling feature selection method, improving prediction accuracy notably. It identifies features such as reserves, month, and Ocean Nino Index in the study. The Random Forest model with Mutual Information-based selection achieved an R2 value of 95%. The research emphasizes the enhanced model accuracy in spot energy price prediction using Mutual Information-based feature selection. Future research should focus on cross-validation techniques and the impact of temporal data for further improvements.

articleTitle: A NARX-AMB Hybrid Approach for Reduced-Order Modeling of a MIMO Heating-Pressing Process
abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid approach that combines the regression neural network and the Associative-Memory-Based (AMB) methods for developing a reduced-order model, with physically interpretable parameters, of a MIMO heating-pressing process within a fishmeal plant. Evaluating multiple AMB structures remains computationally difficult due to the unknown system delay, so this structural exploration is conducted within the framework of the NARX (Nonlinear AutoRegressive with eXogenous inputs) model, which, despite having a significantly higher number of parameters, exhibits ease and speed of training compared to AMB modeling. To address this, we propose a three-step approach: (1) Decomposition of MIMO into SISO Subsystems to focus on individual components. (2) NARX Modeling for SISO Subsystems where we explore different neural network configurations, including the number of hidden neurons and the lag time, using the Bayesian information criteria. (3) Integration of AMB Method using the delay time obtained in step 2. To computationally validate this approach, we utilize real data of a heating-pressing process. This model confirms a clear dependence of the model's parameters on specific regressors.

articleTitle: Analysis of Urban Displacements in Pandemics Using CovWay and GIS Applications
abstract: During pandemics, urban displacements were crucial for social distancing and mobilization efforts to prevent infection. Thus, the goal of this study was to develop the CovWay application, which made it possible to gather data from 35 individuals in pandemics to understand new behavioral patterns. A spatial interpolation methodology was used for the processing and cleaning of GIS data to extract the forms of mobility that were used, as well as the travel routines in 10 days. The findings allowed us to understand the importance of the use of technologies as applications in pandemic scenarios where it is difficult to obtain information due to the norms of physical and social distancing. The commute monitoring methodology allows for estimates of preferences, both in terms of routes and forms of mobility.

articleTitle: An Efficiency Comparison of Cost Functions for FCS - MPC in a Three-phase Inverter
abstract: This work addresses the problem of semiconductor losses in three-phase VSI using Finite Control Set - Model Predictive Control (FCS-MPC). Modifications to the FCS-MPC are proposed to reduce the switching frequency and improve efficiency, and these are tested through simulations. Issues such as switching frequency variability and harmonic distortion are addressed. The proposed solutions, such as delay compensation and cost function optimization, demonstrate notable reductions in the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and the average switching frequency, managing to find a switching reduction of up to 45% in the latter. The research also includes a detailed comparison between SiC-Mosfet and Si-IGBT, highlighting the advantages of the former in efficiency and static and dynamic properties. Despite certain limitations in the SiC-Mosfet, the results show its superiority in high-frequency and high-temperature applications, obtained through a simulation and comparison that considers different aspects, from the switching frequency to the useful life and the packaging.

articleTitle: Customer Churn Prediction in E-Commerce base Using Machine Learning and LIME Algorithm
abstract: Anticipating customer churn trends is extremely important in the current competitive scenario. This allows the company to take preventive measures before churn occurs, as acquiring a new customer can cost up to five times more than retaining an existing customer. Furthermore, understanding the reasons that lead to churn in different scenarios is essential to creating an effective strategy to meet each customer's needs. The present work aims to apply a methodology that combines machine learnin g techniques to enable the anticipation of churn trends and group customers with common motivations. The methodology applied consisted of the following steps: developing a predictive churn model, applying the LIME (Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations) interpretability technique to identify the most influential characteristics in decisions in prone customers and, finally, using K-means clustering to group customers according to their common motivations. This methodology was successfully applied on an e-commerce basis, reaching an area under curve parameter (AVC) of 78% and the creation of 5 final clusters. This approach makes a methodological contribution to future studies and practical experiments in the field of churn analysis.

articleTitle: Shaping the Future of Fog Computing Economics: A Systematic Review of the Most Important Business Models
abstract: Fog Computing, which decentralizes the computing infrastructure and extends cloud capabilities closer to the network edge, emerges as a solution to this challenge. In this paper, the authors review the relevant critical business models of Fog Computing from an economic point of view through business models in different scenarios. Specifically, we will describe the economic interaction of the significant players in the Fog Computing markets: End users, service providers, infrastructure providers, and edge resource owners. The results obtained in this research show that, first, the principal business models depend on infrastructure providers, service providers, and end users' requirements. Second, this review's future issues and opportunities are compelling tradeoff management, adapting to end-user dynamic conditions, and architecture standardization and transparency. Third, the analysis conducted in this article shows the vital role of business model analysis in developing the Fog Computing market based on different architectures, to foster competition and stakeholder collaboration, which will significantly impact the future development of Fog Computing.

articleTitle: The Security Architecture Based on Blockchain for Peruvian Commercial SMEs
abstract: Peruvian SMEs in the commercial sector face increasing vulnerability in their data security, highlighting the lack of effective measures to protect sensitive information. Therefore, this study proposes a blockchain-based security architecture for SMEs, ensuring the immutability and transparency of data, thereby mitigating the risks associated with the manipulation or leakage of confidential information. This architecture consists of 8 layers (Client, Application, Data, Blockchain, Communications, Control, Physical, and Network). For the proposal, it was implemented in a commercial sector SME in Lima, and a perception survey was conducted with 5 security experts. The evaluation results, carried out using the Likert scale, highlighted that the proposed architecture stands out for its high ease of implementation and its ability to improve efficiency in digital asset management, as well as its effectiveness in reducing security risks. The proposed architecture comprehensively ensures information security for commercial SMEs.

articleTitle: A Double Deep Q-Learning Network-Based Path Planning Approach for Autonomous Mobile Robots in Mining Environments
abstract: Motion planning comprises one of the main corner-stones in autonomous mobile robotics, where obstacle avoidance and path planning efficiency are quintessential for the success of maneuverability applications. However, real-time implemen-tation of path planning is limited by adaptive scenarios, high dimensional maps, and time constraints. This paper proposes a Double Deep Q-Network approach for path planning and obstacle avoidance of skid-steer mobile robots due to its ability to explore an extended navigation workspace, and to reduce over estimation bias produced by sparse rewards. The proposed DDPG approach was compared to Q-Iearning and Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithms to examine path planning performance under changing simulation environments, intended to be similar to those found in mining. Results from several exploration trails show that DDQN enhances the path length and significantly outperforms QL and DQN regarding path following time, reducing it about 26 % and 17 %, respectively. Ongoing research is expected to have an impact on the energy resources of the robot in mining scenarios.

articleTitle: A Skills-Based Approach to Policy Creation in Environment Evolution Learning
abstract: This work presents a reinforcement learning method of generating discrete skills while evolving environments in a system. We present a method for determining when to create new skills, how to characterize unknown skills and expand both the actual capability and confidence in these abilities for a reinforcement learning agent. We provide an example wherein many diverse environments for the Bipedal Walker are generated using Uber's POET (Paired Open-Ended Trailblazer) and are then combined with an example world model to derive a relatively small library of skills capable of solving most generated environments. The skills-based approach solves over 85% of the solvable generated environments with an 80-fold reduction in the number of policies required and an exponential reduction in CPU hours used for training.

articleTitle: On the Multivariable Control of a Three-Level Flying Capacitor Buck DC-DC Converter
abstract: In this article, multivariable control strategies are developed for a three-level flying capacitor buck DC-DC converter, tailored for electric vehicle powertrain applications. The work presents a linearization of the Continuous Time Averaged Model of the converter in state space and transfer function matrix. Additionally, it introduces a multi-input multi-output control time-domain design using a Linear Quadratic Integral approach based on this linearized model. Further, a frequency-domain design for structured multi-input multi-output control is proposed, utilizing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathcal{H}_{\infty}$</tex> loop-shaping derived from a mixed-sensitivity approach. Each methodology is elaborated with corresponding simulation results, showcasing the effectiveness of the control strategies. The paper methodically progresses from model development and linearization through control design and performance analysis, providing a thorough examination of the dynamic control of the converter, and its capabilities within a multivariable framework.

articleTitle: Optimizing Energy Storage Systems Deployment in Smart Grids
abstract: The Internet of Smart Grid Things (IoSGT) is recognized as a promising solution to enhance smart grid (SG) ap-plications. Meanwhile, the strategic deployment and scheduling of Energy Storage System (ESS) capacity are crucial for enhancing the performance, resilience, and robustness of IoSG T ecosystems. To reduce peak loads, improve power profiles, and minimize losses in the system, this paper presents the ELOCESS (Effective Location and Optimal Capacity of the ESS) framework within the IoSG T architecture, showcasing innovative contributions to smart grid operations. Leveraging the Time Domain Power Flow (TDPF) alongside Complex-Valued Neural Networks (CVNN), ELOCESS accurately assesses and forecasts voltage fluctuations over time within the IoSGT. In addition, the Plant Growth Simulation Algorithm (PGSA) is adopted to compute the optimal storage location and capacity. Through extensive simulation studies on a standard 33-node network, the efficacy of the ELOCESS approach in identifying the precise location and size of battery storage systems is convincingly demonstrated, which shows an excellent result of optimization techniques by 97.32 %.

articleTitle: Potato Crop Irrigation System in Peru Based on IoT and Machine Learning
abstract: The growing water scarcity in agriculture poses a critical challenge directly impacting the production of essential crops such as potatoes. This paper proposes an automated irrigation system that utilizes IoT technologies and machine learning to optimize water consumption. This system provides real-time access to irrigation information and offers the possibility of remotely activating the water valve. This combination of functionalities not only simplifies the irrigation process but also optimizes water usage. The system was validated through a case study in two orchards, each measuring 4.85 square meters, and using two 210-liter water containers, over a period of 126 days. The results show an MSE, MAE, and R2 of 1.3E-17, 3.3E-09, and 1.0 respectively, achieving a 24.4% reduction in water consumption, equivalent to 343 liters. These findings not only provide a technological solution for water management in agriculture but also support the environmental sustain ability of the agricultural sector by mitigating water scarcity in farming.

articleTitle: Mass Movement Risk Assessment with Drone and GPS Technology: A Case Study in Quito, Ecuador
abstract: This research was carried out to analyse the susceptibility of mass movements in the surroundings of the Las Monjas River and to check the usefulness of drone and GPS technologies, using a drone that allowed us to take approximately 80 aerial photographs per flight, a differential GPS was then used, for which eight control points and a base were placed in order to collect the data at those points. Finally, the data obtained from the GPS and the photographs obtained from the drone were processed to obtain the Digital Surface Model. We create a velocity model with the coordinates to see the soil's behaviour in the study area. Therefore, this work is of great importance due to the incidence of landslides in the city. For these reasons, in sectors next to streams and slopes, preventive actions are recommended for which the respective studies should be carried out in order to identify the areas susceptible to this type of instability and provide accurate information to the population and the competent bodies that can help to reduce the effects of this phenomenon.
